claim: Splenic dendritic cells (DCs) present blood-borne antigens to lymphocytes to promote T cell and antibody responses.
source_text: Splenic dendritic cells (DCs) present blood-borne antigens to lymphocytes to promote T cell and antibody responses.
evidence_reasoning: This is an established function of splenic DCs in the immune system, representing general scientific knowledge in the field.

claim: CD4+ DCs highly express EBI2.
source_text: Here we show that CD4 + DCs highly express EBI2
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B,C demonstrating EBI2 expression levels in CD4+ DCs.

claim: CD4+ DCs migrate to the oxysterol ligand 7α,25-OHC.

evidence_reasoning: This is supported by migration assay data shown in Figure 1D demonstrating CD4+ DC migration in response to 7α,25-OHC.

claim: In mice lacking EBI2, CD4+ DCs are reduced in frequency.

claim: In mice lacking enzymes needed for generating normal distributions of 7α,25-OHC, CD4+ DCs are reduced in frequency.

claim: CD4+ DCs in EBI2-deficient mice fail to situate in marginal zone bridging channels.

evidence_reasoning: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data in Figure 3 showing mislocalization of 33D1+ DCs in EBI2-deficient mice.

claim: The CD4+ DC deficiency can be rescued by LTβR agonism.
source_text: The CD4 + DC deficiency can be rescued by LTβR agonism.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by experimental data in Figure 5B,C showing restoration of CD4+ DC numbers following LTβR agonist antibody treatment.

claim: EBI2-mediated positioning in bridging channels promotes DC encounter with blood-borne particulate antigen.
source_text: EBI2-mediated positioning in bridging channels promotes DC encounter with blood-borne particulate antigen.

claim: Upon exposure to antigen, CD4+ DCs move rapidly to the T-B zone interface.
source_text: Upon exposure to antigen, CD4 + DCs move rapidly to the T-B zone interface

claim: CD4+ DCs promote induction of helper T cell and antibody responses.

claim: EBI2 plays an essential role in CD4+ DC positioning and homeostasis.
source_text: These findings establish an essential role for EBI2 in CD4 + DC positioning and homeostasis
evidence_reasoning: This conclusion is inferred from multiple experimental findings showing DC mispositioning and reduced numbers in EBI2-deficient mice.

claim: EBI2 plays an essential role in facilitating capture and presentation of blood-borne particulate antigens.

evidence_reasoning: This is supported by data showing reduced antigen capture (Figure 6) and impaired immune responses (Figure 7) in EBI2-deficient mice.
